messages:
nate (Procure): Heads-up: EmbarkMetrics sent renewal + new line "data egress surcharge" and weird prorate language. Putting here for quick eyes before I respond.

lena (Finance): Surcharge? paste the invoice snippet. we need landed cost ASAP.

nate (Procure): Snippet from quote: 
```
Service commit: $31,000/mo (1.8B tokens)
Overage: $0.013/1k
Data egress surcharge: 0.5% of monthly invoice (applies to EU region)
Proration: first and last months prorated to daily tokens; invoices final settled at quarter true-up
```
They also want a separate VAT-handling annex if we opt into EU region.

diego (Platform): Tech Qs: is egress surcharge tied to outbound payload size or to billed tokens? If it's % of invoice it's effectively an extra tax we can't control. Also, how do they calculate daily proration for events crossing UTC boundaries?

lena (Finance): If it's % of invoice that adds variability. Nate 1 ask: can they cap/eliminate surcharge or convert to flat fee? Also confirm whether surcharges apply to committed portion or only overage lines.

nate (Procure): Messaged sales: "Confirm: what base does egress surcharge apply to (tokens billed, bytes transferred, or total invoice)? Can surcharge be capped (e.g., max $500/mo) or removed for enterprise customers? Do proration calculations use customer timezone or UTC? Also supply sample pro-forma invoice for a mid-month start and for quarter true-up."

billing-bot: BillingOps note: last EmbarkMetrics invoice INV-2026-06 had a 11% mismatch vs our usage (ticket #2042). That was partly due to rounding on daily prorates.

marta (Legal): Also flag contract language: ambiguous proration + surcharge = risk. We should require explicit caps and an exact formula for proration. Add right to a post-invoice reconciliation with credits if vendor misapplies proration. No surprise fees.

nate (Procure): Vendor replied: "Egress surcharge is 0.5% of total invoice for EU-hosted deployments and applies to full invoice (commit + overage). We can cap surcharge at $600/mo for enterprise customers with a 12-month commit. Proration uses UTC daily buckets. We will provide sample pro-forma invoices on request."

diego (Platform): UTC daily buckets ok but need to ensure our ingestion/event timestamps align; else we'll see discrepancies. Request they expose the proration snippet: pseudo-code or SQL showing daily bucket math.

lena (Finance): Can someone run quick sensitivity: baseline 1.2B tokens -> commit $31k -> surcharge 0.5% = $155/mo extra (not huge) but with VAT/reseller it grows. If cap at $600 even in worst-case it's acceptable. Also need to see pro-forma for mid-month start and the quarterly true-up effect.

marta (Legal): Add contract clause: "vendor will provide pro-forma invoices for any contract start/stop scenarios; vendor guarantees reconciliation tolerance <=2% on proration math or issues automatic credit; surcharge capped at $600/mo unless approved by customer in writing." Also request indemnity for incorrect tax handling and right to audit redacted proration logs quarterly.

nate (Procure): Sales offered a 45-day POC with 75% credit on usage for first 30 days and to waive surcharge during POC. They also provided a sample pro-forma: https://redwood.internal/sheets/embarkmetrics-proforma (internal).

billing-bot: Ops note: reconciliation automation can handle UTC-bucketed proration if vendor provides CSV/parquet with daily billed tokens and rounding rules. Ticket #2042 assigned to ops to validate sample.

diego (Platform): I'll ingest their sample pro-forma and run our reconcile on last 30 days. If their daily buckets match our internal counts within +/-3% we'll be OK.

lena (Finance): I'll model commit vs metered with surcharge and with reseller/VAT scenarios once pro-forma is in. Nate 1 confirm surcharge cap in writing before signing.

nate (Procure): Will push for written cap + waiver during POC + explicit proration formula + quarterly reconciliation clause. TL;DR: surcharge small but opaque; require cap and auditability. If vendor refuses cap then prefer metered with hard overage ceiling.
